titre: Your child's mutuelle and top-up health insurance
resume: What the CSSM (Caisse de sécurité sociale de Mayotte, Mayotte's social security fund) reimburses, what you still pay, how to cover your child with a mutuelle or the C2S, and how to organize things after a separation.
aQuoiCaSert: In Mayotte, health insurance (the CSSM) reimburses part of the cost of care. The rest, called the ticket modérateur (patient's share), is paid by you or by your top-up health insurance (mutuelle). A child is usually covered as a dependent (ayant droit) on one parent's contract. Since 2024, the complémentaire santé solidaire (C2S, free or low-cost top-up health insurance) also exists in Mayotte for low-income households.
quiEstConcerne: Employed parents covered by a company top-up health insurance who want to add their child to it.
Parents who have an individual mutuelle.
Separated parents who need to decide which contract covers the child.
Low-income households, who may be entitled to the C2S.
aSavoir: Visit to a general practitioner: the CSSM reimburses 70%; the remaining 30% is paid by you or your top-up insurance (Cleiss, the French agency for international social security liaison).
At the centre hospitalier de Mayotte (Mayotte's hospital) and its clinics (dispensaires), the insured person pays nothing upfront for consultations and hospital stays, according to the Cleiss.
Some situations are covered at 100%, for example long-term conditions (affections de longue durée) and pregnant women from the 6th month.
Children's coverage depends on your contract: read the information notice given by your employer or your mutuelle.
If your income is low, the C2S covers the whole family, children included: see the dedicated guide entry.
